intelligence.human_view: This is the Real Object Law sharpened into a rule, and the test he gives for it is the zoom: look close, and if you are disappointed, it is not done. A button that reads as real at arm's length and flat when you zoom in was never a real object — it was a picture of one. The inner icon is the cherry on top: it is the smallest thing on the page and the most-touched, and grey, flat, illegible inner icons are what make the whole page feel unfinished even when the big boards are right. White, multi-layered, and representative — you can see what the icon is, and it means what it sits on. Flatness is a defect, wherever it is, and the rule has no exceptions: all the way through. The Hub eye-notes fix round carries this law.
intelligence.simple_view: Nothing flat anywhere! Every little picture and button has to be a real thing you could touch — with layers, like a little cake, not a flat sticker. And the tiny picture inside should be white, not grey, and you should be able to see what it is — like the cherry on top of the cake!
intelligence.grandma_view: Nothing flat anywhere, dear! Every little picture and button has to be a real thing you could touch — with layers, like a little cake, not a flat sticker. And the tiny picture inside should be white, not grey, and you should be able to see what it is — like the cherry on top of the cake, love!
intelligence.naya_view: NO FLATNESS — ALL THE WAY THROUGH. NOTHING FLAT, ANYWHERE. EVERY ICON, EVERY BUTTON, EVERY TILE, EVERY CONTROL — A REAL OBJECT, ELEVATED, MULTI-LAYERED, WITH DEPTH. WHEN YOU ZOOM IN, YOU'RE NOT DISAPPOINTED. THE INNER ICONS ARE WHITE, NOT GREY — MULTI-LAYERED, LEGIBLE, REPRESENTATIVE OF WHAT THEY'RE ON. THE CHERRY ON TOP.
